gloss: sacred object of worship enshrined in a Shinto shrine

definitions.gloss: sacred object; object of worship; divine body
definitions.explanation: A physical object enshrined in a Shinto shrine that is believed to house or represent a deity (kami). Common examples include mirrors, swords, jewels, stones, and natural objects such as mountains or trees.

examples.japanese: この{神社|じんじゃ}の{御神体|ごしんたい}は{鏡|かがみ}だ。
examples.english: The sacred object of this shrine is a mirror.

examples.japanese: {御神体|ごしんたい}は{一般|いっぱん}の{参拝者|さんぱいしゃ}には{公開|こうかい}されていない。
examples.english: The sacred object is not open to the general public.

examples.japanese: {山|やま}そのものを{御神体|ごしんたい}として{祀|まつ}る{神社|じんじゃ}は{日本各地|にほんかくち}にある。
examples.english: Shrines that enshrine an entire mountain as a sacred object exist throughout Japan.

notes:
A compound of {御|ご} (honorific prefix), {神|しん} (deity), and {体|たい} (body). Literally 'the body of the deity.' The {御|ご} prefix reflects the deep reverence with which these objects are treated.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {御神体|ごしんたい}を{祀|まつ}る: to enshrine the sacred object
- {御神体|ごしんたい}を{拝|おが}む: to worship the sacred object
- {御神体|ごしんたい}が{安置|あんち}されている: the sacred object is enshrined
- {山|やま}を{御神体|ごしんたい}とする: to regard a mountain as the sacred object

TYPES OF 御神体:
- {鏡|かがみ}: mirror (the most common type)
- {剣|つるぎ}: sword
- {玉|たま}: jewel
- {石|いし}: stone
- {山|やま}: mountain (e.g., {三輪山|みわやま} at {大神神社|おおみわじんじゃ})

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {御神体|ごしんたい} is typically kept hidden in the innermost sanctuary ({本殿|ほんでん}) of a shrine and is rarely, if ever, shown to the public. This secrecy itself is part of Shinto tradition — the unseen nature of the object reinforces its sacred status. The concept reflects the Shinto belief that {神|かみ} can dwell in physical objects and natural phenomena.
